minutes.headline: Sewer Commission moved to approve a Weston Sampson house-inspection proposal to find sump pumps feeding the sewer.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a revised Weston Sampson proposal for inspecting homes in the Grand Street area for sump pumps and other inflow connections, and a motion to go ahead was put to a voice vote. It also reviewed generator maintenance proposals, the SCADA upgrade quotes, Lake Whalom and Pratt Street betterment outreach, capacity fees and the budget to be presented to the FinCom. February minutes were taken up.

what_happened.line: The commission heard a revised Weston Sampson proposal to inspect homes for sump pumps and other inflow connections, and a motion to proceed went to a voice vote.
The vote result was not audible in the recording, so the outcome is not confirmed in the minutes.
The commission asked Hall Pump for a single total-package quote with an equipment list, due at the next meeting in two weeks.
On generators, the commission chose to seek a prorated proposal for major maintenance first and fold it into the operating contract later.
A balanced sewer budget with no rate increase is to be presented to the FinCom.

why_it_matters: Water from sump pumps entering the sewer is billed as excess flow sent to Fitchburg, so if it is not found, sewer rates could rise substantially for ratepayers.
The no-increase sewer budget going to the FinCom depends in part on how much excess flow is found and how capacity is paid for over 20 years.
watch_next: The next Sewer Commission meeting in two weeks, where a Hall Pump total-package quote is expected.
The FinCom presentation of the sewer budget, and confirmation of the inspection vote in the approved minutes.
